concept.name: Divide & Conquer Algorithms
concept.tagline: Decompose problems into independent subproblems, solve recursively, and combine results for merge sort, quickselect, and parallel speedups.

spark.summary: Divide & conquer splits input, solves subproblems recursively, and merges partial answers—classic examples include merge sort and binary search on answer space.
spark.keyTakeaway: Look for independent subranges or subtrees; combine steps must be efficient or parallelism gains disappear.

concept.whyItMatters: It is the backbone of efficient sorting, closest-pair geometry, and many parallel algorithms.
whenNotToUse: Heavy overlapping subproblems without memoization (use DP instead)
Tiny inputs where recursion overhead dominates

examples.title: Merge sort
examples.scenario: Sort 10M records on a single machine with predictable memory access.
examples.outcome: O(n log n) time with stable ordering.

tradeOffs.con: Stack overflow on huge inputs without care

failureModes.name: Quadratic combine
failureModes.description: Merge/combine step re-scans entire input each level.
failureModes.mitigation: Use linear merges and index pointers.

commonMistakes: Using divide & conquer when subproblems overlap heavily

deepDive.markdownContent:
## Pattern

Split, conquer, combine. Analyze with recurrences and watch the combine step.

relationships.description: Merge sort is the canonical divide & conquer sort.
